title: SR Latch: Two NOR Gates Remember a Bit
topic: Cross-coupled NOR gates form a bistable element. S=1 sets Q=1; R=1 resets Q=0; S=R=0 holds the stored state via the feedback loop.

beats.narration: Two gates with their outputs wired into each other's inputs. That's a memory cell — but how?

elements.content: Two NOR gates, cross-coupled — that's a bit of memory.

beats.narration: Here's the SR latch: two NOR gates cross-coupled. S sets the latch, R resets it, and Q and Q-bar are the outputs — wired back into each other's inputs.

elements.content: Top NOR gate with S input and another input from Q-bar; outputs Q
Bottom NOR gate with R input and another input from Q; outputs Q-bar
Feedback wires Q -> bottom and Q-bar -> top
S, R input labels and Q, Q-bar output labels
the outputs hold each other in place

beats.narration: Raise S to one and the top NOR sees a one — its output Q-bar goes to zero. That zero feeds the bottom NOR with R also zero — bottom output Q swings to one. Q is set.

elements.content: S = 1 highlighted in amber on the top input
Top NOR glows; pulse travels along its output wire to Q-bar = 0
Feedback wire Q-bar=0 -> bottom NOR; bottom glows; Q swings to 1

beats.narration: Now drop S and raise R to one. The bottom NOR sees a one, so Q goes to zero. That zero feeds the top NOR with S also zero — Q-bar swings to one. Q is reset.

elements.content: R = 1 highlighted in rose on the bottom input
Bottom NOR glows; pulse to Q = 0; feedback to top
Top NOR glows; Q-bar swings to 1

beats.narration: And when both S and R are zero, the loop holds whatever Q already was. Pulse S, pulse R, and you can see Q latch high and stay there until R clears it.

elements.content: Timing diagram with rows S, R, Q over a sweep cursor
S pulse at t=1; R pulse at t=3; Q latches high after S, returns to 0 after R
S=R=0 → Q stays. That's the one bit of memory.
